verdicts.evidence: Alston & Bird: RadioShack "will destroy the majority of the data"; agreement "greatly limits the other types of data that can be included in the sale". It does not say payment details or purchase histories were destroyed. PCWorld: no card numbers, SSNs, birth dates or phone numbers "will be transferred", and the deal "removes 14 data fields from the transaction information", leaving seven, so some transaction data did transfer. The FTC release (18 May) predates the deal and does not describe its terms.
verdicts.fix: Most other data was to be destroyed; no card numbers, Social Security numbers, birth dates or phone numbers went to the buyer, and transaction records were cut from 21 fields to seven.

verdicts.evidence: Insurance Journal: customers "remain free to delete their accounts and data at any time". SC Media: 1.9 million deletion requests.

Inference claims more than its facts allow. Toysmart's list was ordered destroyed without being transferred (ClickZ, Out-Law), so on the record read the Toysmart promise was not broken; and 23andMe's case turned on state law and policy compliance, not a never-share promise.
verdicts.source_read: https://www.internetnews.com/marketing/settlement-reached-in-toysmart-list-case (syndicated copy of the ClickZ piece, 12 Jan 2001) ; https://pinsentmasons.com/out-law/news/judge-approves-destruction-of-toysmart-personal-data ; https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/west/2025/07/09/830859.htm
